# rustymath


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

Rustymath provides fast elementary and special functions, statistics, searching and sorting, random sampling, linear algebra, optimization, polynomials and exact arithmetic in Rust and Python. It is the numerical core of [BasedPL](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/).

The Python package needs no NumPy. Its eager operations use the same broadcasting, selection and tolerant-comparison rules as the shared Rust core. For richer array notation, operators and fusion, use BasedPL.

Float functions target four units in the last place (ulps), with [documented exceptions](https://answerdotai.github.io/rustymath/accuracy.html). Rustymath prioritizes speed over last-bit agreement and reproducibility.

## Install

``` sh
pip install rustymath
```

Rust users can add the crate to `Cargo.toml`. See [Using rustymath from Rust](https://answerdotai.github.io/rustymath/rust.html) for scalar and slice forms, build settings, accuracy and speed.

``` python
import rustymath as rm
```

## Arrays and indexing

Functions take Python numbers, nested lists, rustymath arrays or buffer exporters such as NumPy arrays. Broadcasting aligns leading axes. A two-item vector adds one value to each row of this matrix:

``` python
rm.add([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]], [10, 20])
```

    Array([[11, 12, 13], [24, 25, 26]], dtype=int64)

[Arrays and indexing](https://answerdotai.github.io/rustymath/arrays.html) covers construction, dtypes, selection, reshaping, axis names, keys and interoperability.

## Maths and statistics

Real and complex functions operate on whole arrays. The `rustymath.mathish` namespace provides J-inspired [Mathish conventions](https://answerdotai.github.io/rustymath/math.html#mathish-mode). Ordinary comparisons are exact:

``` python
rm.exp([0., 1, 2]), rm.equal(0.1 + 0.2, 0.3)
```

    (Array([1.0, 2.7182818, 7.3890561], dtype=float64), False)

[Maths and statistics](https://answerdotai.github.io/rustymath/math.html) covers elementary and special functions, reductions, scans, statistics and tolerant comparison.

## Searching, sorting and selection

`unique` retains first-occurrence order and reports each value’s position, class number and count:

``` python
rm.unique([3, 1, 3, 2])
```

    Unique(values=Array([3, 1, 2], dtype=int64), firsts=Array([0, 1, 3], dtype=int64), numbers=Array([0, 1, 0, 2], dtype=int64), counts=Array([2, 1, 1], dtype=int64))

[Searching, sorting and selection](https://answerdotai.github.io/rustymath/search.html) distinguishes tolerant matching from exact ordering.

## Random numbers and distributions

Distributions provide density, cumulative probability, quantiles and seeded sampling:

``` python
normal = rm.distribution.normal()
normal.cdf([-1.96, 0, 1.96]), normal.sample(3, seed=0)
```

    (Array([0.024997895, 0.5, 0.9750021], dtype=float64),
     Array([0.11623959, -0.78285485, -2.3346353], dtype=float64))

[Random numbers and distributions](https://answerdotai.github.io/rustymath/random.html) covers sampling and probability functions.

## Linear algebra

Solve real or complex systems, including least-norm solutions for singular or non-square matrices:

``` python
rm.linalg.solve([[4., 1], [1, 3]], [1., 2])
```

    Array([0.090909091, 0.63636364], dtype=float64)

[Linear algebra](https://answerdotai.github.io/rustymath/linalg.html) covers matrix products, reusable factorizations, decompositions and least squares.

## Optimization and iterative solves

Minimize functions, fit residuals or find roots. Here Brent’s method finds where cos x = x:

``` python
rm.optimize.root_scalar(lambda x: rm.cos(x) - x, [0, 1]).root
```

    0.7390851350713886

[Optimization and iterative solves](https://answerdotai.github.io/rustymath/optimize.html) also covers matrix-free linear systems.

## Polynomials, exact arithmetic and number theory

Polynomial coefficients start from the constant term. Factorization accepts Python integers of any size:

``` python
rm.polynomial.polyroots([-6, 11, -6, 1]), rm.number_theory.factor(2**64 + 1)
```

    (Array([(1+0j), (2-0j), (3+0j)], dtype=complex128),
     [(274177, 1), (67280421310721, 1)])

[Polynomials, exact arithmetic and number theory](https://answerdotai.github.io/rustymath/exact.html) includes rational matrix solves and calculations with [`fractions.Fraction`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/fractions.html#fractions.Fraction).

## Accuracy and speed

The Rust page’s [Accuracy and speed](https://answerdotai.github.io/rustymath/rust.html#accuracy-and-speed) section compares each function’s speed with Rust’s standard library. It also explains how the 4-ulp bound holds for `f16`, with and without fused multiply-add, and for `pow` and `root`.
